stories.headline: Over 200,000 march in Amsterdam against Israel's war on Gaza
body: More than 200,000 people marched in Amsterdam, Amnesty's Dutch branch said.
They called for tighter trade limits on Israel and an end to arms sales.
Many wore red for the 'Red Line' protest.
stories.vc: Pressure for trade limits could affect European companies doing business with Israel.

stories.headline: Train crash near Cairo kills seven, injures over 125
body: A train crash in Egypt's Giza province killed at least seven people and injured more than 125.
A Giza-Fayoum train hit the back of another heading to Aswan.
Over 70 ambulances helped move the injured.
stories.vc: Repeated crashes add pressure on Egypt to speed up railway upgrades.

stories.headline: US launches task force to cut Iran's weapons supply routes
body: The US military launched Task Force Iron Gate to block Iran's land routes and Caspian Sea shipments.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards announced plans for underground missile and drone factories.
Fears of a new escalation are growing.
stories.vc: More military pressure keeps oil and shipping markets on edge.

stories.headline: Ballari Road won't fully close for Bengaluru's elevated corridor
body: The BDA says Hebbal Flyover and Ballari Road will not fully close during 18 months of work.
Traffic will move with some lane limits and phased diversions.
The corridor is meant to ease traffic to Kempegowda Airport.
stories.joke: Good news: the road stays open. Bad news: it's still Ballari Road.
stories.vc: Faster airport access lifts property values in north Bengaluru.

stories.headline: Karnataka dairy farmers want KMF to run like Amul
body: Farmers asked the state to run KMF on the Amul model with less political interference.
They want more investment in milk collection, cooling and processing.
They also want milk and curd given to children at anganwadis.
stories.joke: Nandini wants to be Amul when it grows up.
stories.vc: A stronger KMF could raise farm incomes and Karnataka's share of the dairy market.

stories.headline: Snap's Specs AR glasses: lighter, still pricey
body: Snap's Specs AR glasses now weigh nearly half what the prototype did, TechCrunch says.
Pre-orders are open after a public launch by CEO Evan Spiegel.
stories.joke: Lighter on the face, heavy on the wallet.
stories.vc: Snap needs Specs to work to build a business beyond ads.
